title: Finite-field randomized determinant test
statement: Let $n,p,k,m$ be natural numbers, with $p$ prime, and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ Boolean matrix whose bipartite graph has a perfect matching. Assume $2n\le 2^k\le p$ and $n^2k\le m$. Choose a uniformly random bit string of length $m$, divide it into consecutive blocks of $k$ bits, and interpret each block as a natural number modulo $p$. Form the matrix over the field with $p$ elements that has these values at the positions where $A$ is $1$, and zero elsewhere. The probability that this matrix has nonzero determinant is at least $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: the bipartite graph represented by $A$ has a perfect matching
